function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
要計算兩個地理坐標之間的坡度（斜率），我們需要知道這兩個點的海拔高度差。請提供以下資訊：

1. **第一個點（40.7128, -74.0060）的海拔高度**（單位：米或英尺）
2. **第二個點（34.0522, -118.2437）的海拔高度**（單位：米或英尺）

如果您已經有了這些高度資料，請告訴我，我就能幫您計算坡度（以度、百分比或比例表示）。
message.reasoning: The user wants to calculate the slope gradient between two points on terrain. They provide coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437). These are lat/long of New York City and Los Angeles. We need to compute slope gradient. But we don't have elevation data. The function signature requires point1 and point2 as arrays of numbers. It also has optional unit param. But we only have lat/lon; no elevation. So we cannot compute slope gradient without elevation difference. We should ask for elevation or clarify that we need elevation data. The user didn't provide elevation. So we should respond asking for elevation values at those coordinates.
